title: Edit Seam Allowance Properties
content: **** Edit seam allowance properties as needed. **** 1. Click the ![Seam Allowance On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59643803941529) **Seam Allowance tool** in the 2D toolbar. 2. Click on the Pattern outline or point where the seam allowance is applied. → Show Seam allowance options in the property editor. 3. Edit the options below as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Custom Seam Allowance** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568492692249) Toggle the pattern's seam allowance editing ability. **Custom Seam Allowance Off** | The seam allowance follows default presets. Editing abilities are disabled. _**📝 Note:** When editing the pattern outline, the seam allowance follows and snaps to the updated pattern outline automatically._ **Custom Seam Allowance On** | Enables full 2D editing abilities on all seam allowances across the entire pattern. _**📝 Note:** When editing the pattern outline, the seam allowance preserves its shape. Press the **F4 key** to refresh the seam allowance by following the new outline._ **Lock Seam Allowance** | Unlock to click and edit the seam allowances. Lock to block from selection or click-actions by 2D editing tools. **Width** | Enter the width of the seam allowance in line or point. **Smooth Intersection** | Click the intersection between the seam allowances of different widths to smoothly connect the seam allowances of the two line segments. **Seam Type** | Select the desired seam type for each seam allowance's start, end, and intersection. The options' activation status depends on the selected point. **Start** | It activates when a seam allowance is created only at the start point. Select the desired seam type among 3 options. **End** | It activates when a seam allowance is created only at the endpoint. Select the desired seam type among 3 options. **Intersection** | It activates when seam allowances are created at both ends of a line. title: Animation Marker
content: ## **New in 2026.0** **** Animation Markers indicate significant points on the timeline or in space, allowing users to quickly identify the locations of scene transitions, events, and keyframes. Comments can be added to Markers to leave notes regarding editing intentions or task instructions. Additionally, they can be utilized as event triggers in the API via their names. #### **Add** 1. Open the **Animation Editor**. 2. Right-click the **Timeline Ruler** to display the context menu. 3. Click **Add** under the Marker group. 4. When the Marker dialog appears, set the name and frame of the Marker, then click OK. 5. Verify that a new Marker has been created at the specified frame. #### #### **Edit** 1. Hover the mouse over a created Marker to view its name and frame through the displayed tooltip. 2. To move a Marker, select and drag it to the left or right. 3. To edit a Marker's name, double-click the Marker or right-click it and select Edit from the context menu. 4. Modify the information in the displayed dialog, then click OK. 5. Verify that the changes have been applied to the Marker. #### #### **Copy and Paste** 1. Select one or more Markers. 2. Copy the Markers by pressing Ctrl+C or clicking Copy from the right-click context menu. 3. Specify the current frame using the playhead, then paste the Markers by pressing Ctrl+V or clicking Paste from the context menu. 4. The Markers will be pasted at the current frame indicated by the playhead. #### #### **Delete** 1. Select one or more Markers you wish to delete. 2. Press the Delete key or click Delete from the right-click context menu to remove the Markers.
content_description: Discover the new Animation Markers feature in 2026.0 that enhances timeline navigation and editing by allowing users to add, edit, copy, and delete markers for scene transitions and events, complete with customizable notes and API integration.

title: Does CLO offer student discounts?
content: **Question** Does CLO offer student discounts? **Answer** Yes, we offer a 50% discount on an Individual plan to eligible high school, college, and university students worldwide. Discounted price will be $25 USD/month or $225 USD/year. **Important Note:** To receive the student discount, you must verify your student status before starting your trial. If you fail to do so, you will not be eligible for the discount. **Student Eligibility** To qualify for a student discount, you must be at least 13 years old and enrolled in one of the following: * University or college - full-time students in an accredited university or college that offers degrees. * Primary or secondary school - full-time students in an accredited primary or secondary school. **Important Note:** The CLO Student Discount is limited to 4 years. If still enrolled after 4 years proof of continued enrollment is required for an additional 2 year extension of the Student Discount once. **I'm eligible. How can I get the student discount?** Please check if your student email is already approved with CLO: [**Student Eligibility Check**](https://clo3d.com/en/student-eligibility) * **When your school domain is already approved** , 1. 1. Add your student email. 2. The **USE EMAIL ADDRESS** button will be activated. Click on the button and create your account. 3. Your account will be automatically applied to the student discount. (You can see the discounted price on your checkout page after the subscription button.) * **If your school domain is not approved or you don't have a student email address,** 1. 1. Go to the [**SIGN UP**](https://style.clo-set.com/en/account/signup?returnUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fclo3d.com%2Fauth%2Fsignin%3FredirectTo%3D%2F) page and select Individual. 2. Create your CLO account using either your student email address (if available) or your personal email address. 3. If using a personal email please provide a letter from your school stating they do not provide students with school email addresses After verifying your account, please [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) and submit one of the following documents: * School ID card with a valid date. * Official enrollment verification statement issued within the last 6 months. * Tuition statement for the current year/semester. Our support team will review your documents and apply for the discount if approved. * **If you already have an account with us,** Simply [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) and submit your proof of enrollment. *Please note that if you can't use your school email after graduation, you would face an issue with receiving CLO emails such as renewal notifications and any CLO news. *
content_description: Discover how eligible students can take advantage of a 50% discount on CLO's Individual plan while ensuring they verify their student status for access.

title: CLO system requirements (April 2026)
content: This document outlines the minimum and recommended system requirements to successfully install, launch, and operate CLO software. ## Windows Category | Minimum | Recommended ---|---|--- **OS** | Windows 11 64-bit (24H2) 1) | Windows 11 64-bit (25H2) **Processor** | AMD® Ryzen™ 3000 series Intel® 8th-Gen series 2) | AMD® Ryzen™ 9000 series or higher Intel® Core™ i9 14th-Gen or higher **Memory** | 16 GB | 64 GB 3) **Graphics card** | AMD, Intel, or Nvidia GPUs supporting OpenGL 1.6 or higher | NVIDIA® GeForce RTX 4000 series or NVIDIA® RTX A, RTX Ada, RTX Pro Blackwell series 4) 5) 6) 7) **Storage** | SSD with 10 GB free space | SSD with 20 GB free space **Display** | 1920x1080 (FHD) | 2560x1440 (QHD) or 3840x2160 (UHD, 4K) **Input device** | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse **Network** | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) Microsoft ended Windows 10 support on October 14, 2025. When setting up a new workstation, we strongly recommend installing Windows 11. [**Learn more**](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/windows-10-support-has-ended-on-october-14-2025-2ca8b313-1946-43d3-b55c-2b95b107f281). 2) CLO's built-in V-Ray renderer requires [**AVX2**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Vector_Extensions) support. Attempting to render using an older processor (e.g., Intel 3rd Gen or earlier), the V-Ray render function will not operate. 3) 16GB RAM is the minimum baseline. Handling heavy, complex garments, animations, or ultra-high-quality rendering, 64GB or more is required to ensure system stability and performance. 4) CLO leverages [**Nvidia CUDA**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA) for GPU acceleration. Using integrated Intel or AMD graphics, simulation and rendering processes will not benefit from hardware acceleration. For optimal performance, an Nvidia GPU is highly recommended. 5) Experiencing graphics-related issues or system instability, verify your GPU drivers are updated to the latest version. Please refer to our [**Graphics Card Troubleshooting Guide**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768). 6) CLO requires [**OpenGL**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenGL) 1.6 or higher. Using certain integrated mobile GPUs (Intel/AMD) that lack full OpenGL support, the software may fail to launch. Verify your GPU's OpenGL compatibility with your hardware manufacturer. 7) High-quality V-Ray rendering and complex simulations are highly resource-intensive, performing these tasks. A GPU with at least 12GB of VRAM is required (4GB minimum for basic usage). * * * ## macOS Category | Minimum | Recommended ---|---|--- **Mac models** | Apple Silicon Mac: M1 1) | Apple Silicon Mac: M2, M3, M4, M5 **macOS** | macOS Sonoma 14 *See notes for dependencies 2) | macOS Sequoia 15, Tahoe 26 **Processor** | Apple Silicon Chip | Apple Silicon Chip 3) **Memory** | 16 GB | 64 GB 4) **Storage** | SSD with 10 GB free space | SSD with 20 GB free space **Display** | 1920x1080 (FHD) | Retina 4K, Retina 5K supported **Input devices** | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse **Network** | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) With Apple's hardware transition, starting with macOS Golden Gate 27, which will be released in the fall of 2026, Intel-powered Macs will no [**no longer be supported**](https://www.wired.com/story/macos-tahoe-last-update-for-intel-macs/). 2) The architectural updates in CLO v2024 and newer, when installing the software, macOS Monterey 12 or later is strictly required. Check your [**Mac's compatibility here**](https://support.apple.com/en-us/103260). 3) Starting with CLO v2025.0 version when running the software on Apple Silicon Macs, V-Ray rendering via GPU acceleration (Metal) is fully supported. [**Learn how to configure V-Ray settings**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties). 4) 16GB RAM is the minimum baseline. Handling heavy, complex garments, animations, or ultra-high-quality rendering, 64GB or more is required to ensure system stability and performance. * * * ## Important Precautions * Note that CLO does not support garment pattern digitizers. * Wacom® products are officially tested and supported. Third-party tablets may experience unexpected compatibility issues. * BootCamp and desktop virtualization applications (e.g., Parallels) are not supported. * 32-bit OS and alternative/mobile operating systems (iOS, Android, Linux, ChromeOS, Windows Mobile) are strictly unsupported. * CLO installers are only provided natively via the [**official CLO website**](https://clo3d.com/en/clo/download/installer) as `.exe` or `.dmg` formats. We do not distribute `.msi` or `.pkg` packages. * Installing CLO in virtual server environments (VM, VDI, or Cloud environment), the software can operate, but the CLO team does not provide official technical support for these architectures. ## See also * [**Disk access rights required when CLO is running**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697-Disk-access-rights-required-when-CLO-is-running) * [**How to Speed Up CLO**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23390057463577-How-to-Speed-Up-CLO) * [**How to Prevent CLO File Corruption**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23206278838681-How-to-Prevent-CLO-File-Corruption) * [**Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting)
content_description: This webpage provides essential system requirements and recommendations for installing and running CLO software effectively on both Windows and macOS platforms.

title: CLO to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content:
This guide outlines the entire workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. * * * ### **⭐1. Project Initialization and Plugin Setup** #### **1-1: Installing Core Data** Ensure you have **Unreal Engine 5.6** or later installed before proceeding. 1. Open the **Epic Games Launcher** and navigate to the **Library** tab. 2. Locate your Unreal Engine installation card. 3. Click the **down arrow** next to the **Launch** button and select **Options**. 4. In the installation options window, check the box next to **MetaHuman Creator Core Data**. 5. Click **Apply** to download and install the required data. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164145945) #### **1-2: Project Configuration** 1. Create or open your Unreal Engine project. 2. Navigate to **Edit > Project Settings** in the main menu. 3. In the left sidebar, scroll down to the **Plugins** section and select **MetaHuman SDK**. 4. Locate the setting labeled **MetaHuman Packaging Paths**. > **⚠️ Warning:** **Do not change the name of this folder path.** Due to a known issue, the workaround currently in place relies on this folder retaining its default name. Modifying it will break the packaging process. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323158561817) #### **1-3: Outfits Directory Setup** By default, the location for Outfits is `/Game/Outfits`. In your **Content Browser** , this path appears as **All > Content > Outfits**. You should create and edit all your Outfit Assets within this directory. **Important for FAB Uploads:** If you plan to use the **MetaHuman Manager** to verify and package your asset for FAB, you must adhere to a strict folder structure: * Your Outfit Asset and **all of its dependencies** must reside in a single subfolder within the `/Game/Outfits` directory. * If assets are scattered outside this specific subfolder, the MetaHuman Manager will fail the verification process, and packaging will be impossible. #### **1-4: Plugin Setup** Make sure to enable **Chaos Cloth Plugins** and **MetaHuman Creator Plugin** , and restart your Unreal Engine project. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164146329) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164146585) * * * ### **⭐2: Preparing MetaHumans for Export (UE 5.6 and later)** #### **2-1: Create and Customize the MetaHuman** 1. In the **Content Browser** , right-click and navigate to **MetaHuman > MetaHuman Character**. 2. Open the newly created MetaHuman asset to enter the editor. 3. Customize the character’s attributes (Face and Body Measurements) as needed. #### **2-2: Configure Assembly Settings** Once customization is complete, prepare the asset for export: 1. Navigate to the **Assembly** tab. 2. Select **Download Textures**. 3. Check the box for **Create Full Rig**. 4. Change the Assembly Target from **UE Cine (Complete)** to **(DCC Export)**. 5. Select your desired **Output Folder**. 6. Click the **Assembly** button to generate the files. > **ℹ️ Integration Note:** Successfully completing this step saves the specific Body and Head files required for **DNA Import in CLO**. You will need this DNA file in the next section to accurately fit garments to your MetaHuman body. * * * ### ⭐**3: Import MetaHuman DNA into CLO (CLO 2025.2 or later)** 1. Launch **CLO**. 2. Navigate to **File > Import > DNA** in the main menu. 3. Browse to the output folder you defined in the previous section. 4. Select the exported **Body** and **Head** files. 5. Click **OK** to complete the import. For more details, please refer to the following CLO manual for more details: [**MetaHuman DNA Importer**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/51821648831257-MetaHuman-DNA-Importer) * * * ### **⭐4: Prepare Garment in CLO and Bake UV Maps** #### **4-1: Garment Simulation** 1. Create a new garment or apply existing garments. 2. Run the Simulation to drape and fit the garments onto the imported MetaHuman body. #### **4-2: UV Preparation** Before exporting, ensure the UV maps are correctly packed to prevent texture issues. 1. Switch the view to the **UV Editor**. 2. Select the **whole garment** (all patterns). 3. Run **UV Packing** to organize the UV islands efficiently. #### **4-3: Exporting to USD files** 1. Navigate to **File > Export > USD**. 2. In the export dialog window, configure the settings exactly as follows: **Setting Category** | **Configuration** ---|--- **Object** | Select **Include Garment** **Patterns** | Choose **Select All Patterns** **Geometry** | Set to **Single Object** **Thickness** | Select **Thick** **Textures** | Check**Unified UV Coordinates** and **Select All Maps** **Simulation** | Check **Include Garment Simulation Data** * * * ### **⭐5: Convert Style into a Resizable MetaHuman Wardrobe Asset** #### **5-1: Prepare Project and Import USD Outfit** **Step 1: Open Your Project** Launch Unreal Engine 5.6 (or later) and open your target project. **Step 2: Establish Directory Structure** You must establish a precise folder hierarchy in the **Content Browser**. This structure is critical for asset validation. 1. Navigate to `/Game/Outfits/`. 2. Create a folder named after your asset (e.g., `Style01`). 3. **Crucial Step:** Inside that folder, create a **subfolder with the exact same name** (`Style01`). Your hierarchy should look like this:
```
Content
└── Outfits ├── Meshes <-- Store MetaHuman (MH) skeletal files here └── Style01 <-- Main Asset Folder └── Style01 <-- Working Folder (Import USDs here)
``` **Folder Purpose Definitions:** * **Meshes:** Dedicated storage for MetaHuman skeletal and mesh files. * **Main Folder (e.g., Style01):** This parent folder will eventually contain _only_ the finalized wardrobe asset. * **Working Folder (e.g., Style01/Style01):** This is your workspace. All development, importing, and editing must take place here. You may organize subfolders inside this directory as needed. **Step 3: Export the MetaHuman Reference Mesh** You need the skeletal mesh from your MetaHuman to serve as a reference. 1. Navigate to your MetaHuman asset location. 2. Locate the **Skeletal Mesh** for the body (not the Blueprint). 3. Right-click the asset and select **Asset Actions > Export**. 4. Save this file to the `Outfits/Meshes` folder you created in Step 2. **Step 4: Import the USD Outfit** 1. Navigate to your working folder: `Outfits > Style01 > Style01`. 2. Import your USD outfit file into this folder. 3. In the **USD Import Options** dialog, leave all settings at their **Default** values and click **Import**. Unreal Engine will automatically generate subfolders for _Textures_ , _Materials_ , and _Static Meshes_. Locate and double-click the **Static Mesh** of the outfit to open it. **🔧 Troubleshooting: Transparency Issues** If your garment appears transparent or ghostly in the viewport, follow these steps to fix the material blend mode: 1. In the details panel or content browser, find the material applied to the mesh. 2. Right-click the material instance and select **Find Parent**. 3. Open the Parent Material. 4. Scroll down to the **Material Property Overrides** section. 5. Locate **Blend Mode**. 6. Change the dropdown from **Translucent** to **Opaque**. 7. **Save** and **Apply** the material. #### **5-2: Create and Configure Cloth Asset** **Step 1: Create the Cloth Asset** First, you need to generate the base asset files in your project directory. 1. Navigate to your **Working folder**. 2. **Right-click** > **Physics** > **Cloth Asset**. 3. Name the asset clearly (e.g., `CA_Style01`). > **Note:** This automatically creates a **DataFlow node** with a "DF" prefix. This node is required for the asset to function—do not delete or modify it. **Step 2: Open and Clean the Dataflow Graph** Set up the workspace by removing unnecessary simulation nodes. 1. **Right-click** on your new CA Node (`CA_Style01`). 2. Select **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335888520729) 3. **Clean up the graph:** Since you are not running a simulation, delete all nodes **EXCEPT** the following: * `Transfer Skin Weights` * `Remesh` * `ClothAssetTerminal` * _(Optional)_ You may also delete the purple and brown explanatory notes. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335876830233) **Step 3: Import and Connect Static Mesh** Now, import your specific outfit geometry and establish the node connections. 1. **Add Import Node:** Right-click in the graph, type **StaticMeshImport** , and select it. 2. **Configure Node Details** (Bottom-right panel): * **Uncheck:** `Import Sim Mesh` (as you do not have one). * **Static Mesh:** Drag in or select your outfit mesh (e.g., `style01`). 3. **Connect the Nodes:** * Drag from `StaticMeshImport` (**Collection**) → `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**). * Drag from `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**) → `Remesh` (**Collection**). * Drag from `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**) → `ClothAssetTerminal`. * Drag from `Remesh` (**Collection**) → `Collection Lods 1` (on the Terminal node). **Step 4: Configure Skin Weights** Adjust the `TransferSkinWeights` node to map the outfit to the character body correctly. 1. Click on the **TransferSkinWeights** node. 2. Update the **Node Details** panel with the following settings: * **Target Mesh(es):** Change to `Render Mesh`. * **Render Mesh Transfer Source:** Change to `Skeletal Mesh`. * **Transfer Method:** Change to `Closest Point on Surface`. * **Source Asset:** Drag in or select the combined body mesh paired with the garment (e.g., `Character01_CombinedSkelMesh`). **Step 5: Visualize the Asset** Verify your work in the Construction Viewport. 1. Click on the **Remesh** node in the graph. 2. Locate the **Construction Viewport** (the window to the _left_ of the Simulation Viewport). 3. If the viewport is empty: * Click the **View Mode Dropdown** (Top right of the viewport, icon looks like a cube). * Select **Render**. 4. Save Project. #### **5-3: Create and Configure Wardrobe Asset for MetaHuman Creator** **📂Step 1: Organize Folders** Before starting, ensure your file structure is clean to avoid referencing errors. 1. Navigate to your main folder → **Style01**. 2. Ensure this folder contains **only** your **Working folder** (which should be named identically to your intended outfit asset or use the `OA_` prefix). 3. Remove any other loose assets or extraneous folders. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335845173657) **👕Step 2: Create the Outfit Asset** Generate the core asset file using the physics menu. 1. **Right-click** in the folder → **Physics** → **Outfit Asset**. 2. **Name the Asset:** * Must match your folder name exactly. * _Recommended Format:_ `OA_Style01`. 3. **Select Template:** * Choose **Resizable Outfit** when prompted. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335817349529) **📦Step 3: Manage the Dataflow (DF) Node** A dependency node is automatically created and must be stored correctly. 1. Locate the new node prefixed with `DF_`. 2. Drag it into your **Working folder**. 3. Select **Move Here**. > **Note:** This step is required for packaging in Fab and ensuring compatibility with the MetaHuman Manager. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335849553433) **⚙️Step 4: Configure the Dataflow Editor** Open the editor and optimize performance settings before adding heavy assets. 1. **Double-click** your new Outfit Asset (`OA_Style01`) to open the Dataflow Editor. 2. Locate the **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** button in the top toolbar. 3. Click the **three dots** next to it. 4. Select **Manual Graph Evaluation**. * _Why?_ This prevents the engine from trying to process changes after every single click, avoiding long wait times during setup. **🧵Step 5: Add Cloth Assets** Link your Cloth Assets (CA) and Skeletal Meshes to the Outfit Asset. 1. **Dataflow Members Panel** (Bottom Left): * Check the box for **Sized Outfit Source**. * Click the **Plus (+)** sign for each cloth asset you need to add. 2. **Configure Each Entry:** * **Source Asset:** Select your cloth asset (e.g., `CA_Style01`). * **Size Name:** Enter a descriptive name. * **SourceBodyParts:** Add your combined skeletal mesh (e.g., `Character01_combinedSkelMesh`). * **Num Resizing Interpolation Points:** * _Default:_ 1500 * _Recommended Range:_ 1000–2500 * _Tip:_ Higher numbers are more accurate but process slower. 3. **Variable Overrides:** * Switch to the **Dataflow Tab** (Bottom Left). * Find **Variable Overrides** and check the box for **SIZE OUTFIT SOURCE**. * Verify that both the `CA_` asset and the `CombinedSkelMesh` are successfully linked. **⏳Step 6: Evaluate the Graph** Process the data to generate the outfit sizes. 1. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** in the top toolbar. 2. **Wait:** Watch the progress bar as it processes each size. This may take several minutes. 3. **Reset:** Once complete, click the three-dot menu again and turn **Automatic Evaluation** back on. **🔄Step 7: Re-Evaluation (Troubleshooting)** If you modify any input assets later (cloth, static mesh, etc.), you must force a re-evaluation. 1. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph**. 2. **If no progress bar appears:** * Right-click the **Sized Outfit Source** node → **Evaluate**. * _OR_ Right-click the **OutfitAssetTerminal** node → **Evaluate**. **💾Step 8: Save** * **Save your Outfit Asset** to preserve all configurations. **👤Step 9: Test in MetaHuman Creator (MHC)** Verify the outfit works on a character and resizes correctly. 1. **Create Test Character:** * Content Browser → Right-click → **MetaHuman** → **MetaHuman Character**. * Name the character. 2. **Open in MHC:** * Open the character and navigate to the **Hair & Clothing** tab. * Scroll to **Outfit Clothing**. 3. **Apply Outfit:** * Remove the current **Wardrobe Asset**. * Drag your **Outfit Asset** (`OA_Style01`) into this slot. * Double-click to apply. 4. **Test Resizing:** * Use body sliders or apply different presets to ensure the clothing adapts to the body shape. **🧥Step 10: Verify Wardrobe Item** * After applying the outfit, check your Content Browser. * A new asset should appear: `WI_Style01` (Wardrobe Item). * * * ### **⭐6. MetaHuman Outfit Testing Checklist** The following checklist provides quality assurance for the MetaHuman testing phase. Use this to systematically verify that your `OA_` asset resizes correctly without breaking. **1\. Preparation** * [ ] **Clean State:** Ensure the character has no other clothing layers underneath that might cause false clipping positives. * [ ] **Asset Applied:** Verify `OA_Style01` is successfully slotted in the **Outfit Clothing** section. * [ ] **Visibility:** Zoom in close to the garment boundaries (necklines, cuffs, waistbands). **2\. The "Extremes" (Stress Testing)** _This is where most resizing errors occur. If it works here, it usually works everywhere._ * [ ] **Maximum Bulk:** Set sliders/preset to **Tall + Heavy/Overweight**. * _Check for:_ Skin poking through the cloth (clipping) at the stomach, shoulders, and thighs. * [ ] **Minimum Frame:** Set sliders/preset to **Short + Thin/Underweight**. * _Check for:_ "Floating" geometry where the cloth is too far from the skin, or collapsing geometry where the mesh overlaps itself. **3\. Specific Body Regions** _Adjust individual sliders if your interface allows, or select specific presets._ * [ ] **Chest/Bust:** Maximize and minimize. Check for texture stretching or distortion on logos/patterns. * [ ] **Shoulders:** Widen and narrow. Check if straps (if applicable) stay aligned or slide off. * [ ] **Waist/Hips:** Check the transition area. If this is a shirt, ensure it doesn't clip into the pants line (or vice versa). **4\. Visual Inspection Criteria** * [ ] **Clipping:** No skin showing through the fabric. * [ ] **Distortion:** No extreme stretching of the UVs/texture (e.g., plaid patterns looking like spaghetti). * [ ] **Seams:** Ensure the vertices at the seams are not splitting apart during resizing. * [ ] **Neckline:** Ensure the collar doesn't eat into the neck on "Heavy" settings. **5\. Final Verification** * [ ] **Reset to Neutral:** Return to **Average Height + Average Weight**. Does the mesh snap back perfectly? * [ ] **Asset Generation:** Confirm that the `WI_Style01` (Wardrobe Item) exists in the content browser after your tests.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD files and seamlessly integrating them with Unreal Engine's MetaHuman framework.

title: Pattern Drafter
content: **List of Contents** Open Create Pattern Edit Pattern Add Grading AI Pattern Drafter (Beta) **** Easily Create your First Pattern within CLO, using either measurement points or your flat sketches. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45053653355417) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/X0GSGKGGYaM) #### **Open** 1. Click the 2D ▶ **Pattern Drafter** in the top menu. 2. Choose a Pattern Type to start drafting your patterns. **** #### **Create Pattern** 1. Set Measurement provide 3 different options to view and adjust pattern measurements. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **General** | This will give you a complete list of the most commonly used Points of Measure for that style. **Simple** | This will give you the most commonly used points of measure for simple editing of patterns. **Custom** | This is automatically adjust to Custom when you select your own measurement list and customize to your preference. 1\. Click ![setting.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45585774347289) **Setting** button to view the full list of measurements. 2\. Use the checkbox to show or hide items as needed. 3\. Once setup is complete, click ![Total-1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45585774352537) **Exit** button to apply changes. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55681539045401)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59720683251097) 2. If you have an avatar to draft the pattern for, [open the avatar](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002687268-Avatar-AVT-Open-Add-Save) first, then click the ![Match to Avatar.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59720694642713) **Match to Avatar Size** button. * If the button is disabled, restart Pattern Drafter and try again. → The pattern measurements are automatically adjusted to match the avatar's size. **📝 Note:** Currently, this feature is available only for CLO avatars. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55681539045401)** 3. Enter your pattern measurement values. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **![Total.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45585774384537)Total** | Certain Measurements include the Toptal option to input the full front and back circumference. **Base** | Certain measurements include dropdown options, as they are commonly taken from different areas of the pattern. E.g. **\- Total Length:** High Point Shoulder, Or Center Front/ Back **\- Across Front/ Back:** 4", 5" or 6" from High Point Shoulder **\- Across Waist:** 4", 5" or 6" from Armhole **\- Across Bust/ Chest:** Armhole to Armhole or 1" from Armhole **\- Bicep Width:** Armhole to Armhole or 1" from Armhole **Symmetry** | Set the front and back pattern to Symmetry or Half Symmetry ![list.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45586096388121) **Show All Measurement** | View all inactive measurements in each section. 4. Click the ![Create.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55646905944985) button. → When a Parametric Pattern is created to automatically create the [POM](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/360004712034-POM) from the parametric Patterns. **📝****Note** : • Only the defined measurements are generated as 2D POMs and added to the [POM Obejct Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/37542686165529-POM-Object-Browser). • Automatically generated POMs can only be selected with the [Edit POM ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025716814-Edit-2D-POM)tool to check their length. #### **Edit Pattern** Patterns created with Pattern Drafter can be edited while retaining their original parameters. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55681539045401)** **in Pattern Drafter** 1. Open the Pattern Drafter. → If a parametric pattern exists, select whether to create a new pattern or edit it. 2. Select the ![Frame 215.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55673983171865) button. → The pattern type is automatically detected. 3. Change the measurement values, then click the ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55673922190361)**** button. Or, click ![Create as New.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55673983175705) button to generate a new parametric pattern. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55681539045401)** **with Edit POM tool** 1. Click the [**Edit POM**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025716814-Edit-2D-POM)**** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Click a POM within the parametric pattern and enter a value in the length field. → The parametric pattern updates based on the entered value while maintaining its parametric relationships, the same as editing in Pattern Drafter. **📝****Note** : Editing a parametric pattern directly breaks its connection with Pattern Drafter. It is recommended to edit the pattern using Pattern Drafter or the Edit POM tool instead. #### **Add Grading** 1. Click the ![Add Grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55684986671129) **Add Grading** in the Pattern Drafter. 2. Set up the size table for graded patterns, then click the**OK.** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Add** | Add new sizes by clicking ![add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55685003829017) **Add** button. When a size is selected, clicking**Add** inserts a new size above the selected size. **Rename** | Rename a size by double-clicking a size name. **Delete** | Delete a size by clicking a size and pressing the **Delete** key. → Size columns are added to the Measurement table. 3. Enter full measurement values for each size or specify grading increments between sizes. 4. Click the ![Create.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55646905944985) button. → The pattern is graded based on the entered value. _**✨Tip:** _Grading can be adjusted directly with the ![Edit Grading Curve On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55684986679961)****[**Edit Grading**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015798567-Set-Grading#h_01JR7KQV8PQACMKZBJA4J97SNT)**** tool. #### **AI Pattern Drafter (Beta)** Using a Sketch CLO will Automatically generate measurements to create a drafted pattern for you. 1. Click **AI Pattern Drafter (Beta)** button on the top right of the Pattern Drafter. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55681539045401)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59720683251097) 2. If you have an avatar to draft the pattern for, [open the avatar](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002687268-Avatar-AVT-Open-Add-Save) first, then select the Match to Avatar option. * If the button is disabled, restart AI Pattern Drafter and try again. **📝 Note:** Currently, this feature is available only for CLO avatars. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55681539045401)** 2. Generate a background image to be composited by entering prompts or upload it directly. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Text Prompt** | Select the garment type and write in your sketch idea. Make sure to add in as many descriptive words as possible. if you want to emphasize something place it in brackets. **✨ Writing Tips:** Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. ![Comment.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587052844441)**Keyword Suggestions** | Suggested keywords will appear as you type to help you complete your prompt. ![icon_pin_off.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587052847001)**Maintain Prompt** | Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Pattern image is created anew each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while preserving the existing results as much as possible. The results may differ from the existing ones depending on the addition or change of the prompts. ![icon_random_dice.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587052849049) **Random** | Sample prompts are provided randomly ![Editor Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587052849945) **Clear** | Clear anything that was written to restart. **Image** | Click the **Upload** button to add any garment or pattern image. 3. Click ![Generate.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45587052851097) button and an image will be generated for you to choose from. This process can be replicated until you get the desired outcome. Your image history can be found on the right side of the window. → The pattern is drafted automatically to match the avatar's size.

title: Although my hardware has more than 4 CPU Cores, CLO is not as fast as I expected.
content: **Question** Although my hardware has more than 4 CPU cores, CLO is not as fast as I expected. **Answer** CLO's program speed increases with faster Core clock speed and more Cores. However, there is NO significant speed advancement when there are more than 4 Cores compared to the program speed ran with four Cores. Therefore, to be cost-effective, we recommend hardware with four Cores, each Core's speed being between 3.5 ~4.0 Ghz or faster.
content_description: This web page provides insights on optimizing hardware configuration for CLO to achieve the best performance, emphasizing the effectiveness of using four high-speed CPU cores.

content: **List of Contents** Select Move ### **Objective** Select and move graphic. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ **Transform Graphic** ** **2D/ 3D Toolbar ▶****![graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360019467214/graphic.png) **Transform Graphic** ** Operation** **Select** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ **Transform Graphic** ** **2D/ 3D Toolbar ▶****![graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360019467214/graphic.png) **Transform Graphic** 2. title: Customize Toolbar
content: **New in 2026.0** **Group Tools** **Rearrange Tools** **Open/Save** **Reset to Default** **** Customize and rearrange tool groups in the 2D and 3D toolbars for quicker access to the tools you use most. #### **Group Tools** 1. Right-click on the 3D or 2D toolbar and select **Group Tools**. → The Group Tools window opens. 2. Select the toolbar you want to edit (3D or 2D) from the upper-right corner of the Group Tools window. → The current tool group layout and order are displayed as they appear on the toolbar. 3. Drag a tool to a new position within the same group. → The tool order within the group is updated. → The tool placed at the top of the group becomes the default tool displayed on the toolbar. 4. Drag a tool to a different group. → The tool is moved to the selected group. 5. Drag a tool from a group into the empty space between groups. → The tool is separated from its current group and becomes a new group. 6. Click **OK** to apply the changes. → The toolbar reflects the configured groups and tool positions. **📝****Note:** Hide unused tools from the toolbar by clicking the ![Eye Off.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642175807001) **Hide** button next to each tool.**** #### **Rearrange Tools** 1. Right-click on the 3D or 2D toolbar and select **Rearrange Tools**. → Tool rearrangement mode is enabled. 2. Drag a tool to the desired position. * Tools cannot be moved between the 3D and 2D toolbars. #### **Open/Save** 1. Click the **Open** or**Save** button in the lower-left corner of the Group Tools window, or go to Main Menu > Save As/Open » **Tool Set**. → Toolbar group configurations can be saved to and loaded from a JSON file. #### **Reset to Default** 1. Right-click the 3D or 2D toolbar and select Reset to Default. → The toolbar is reset to the default CLO settings. **📝****Note:** Resetting the toolbar cannot be undone. We recommend saving the current configuration to a file before resetting.
content_description: Customize and streamline your workflow by rearranging and managing tool groups in the 2D and 3D toolbars for faster access to your essential tools.

title: Lacing
content: **New in 2026.0** **Define Path** **Edit Lacing** **** Automate the lacing process by guiding the lacing pattern and direction through designated holes. This tool eliminates manual intervention by automatically routing the cord and generating an editable pattern for further customization. **** #### **Define Path** 1. Select the **![Lacing On.svg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55445403327257)****Lacing Tool** from the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click the **starting hole** where the lacing begins or where the cord is first inserted. 3. Click the **next hole** in your desired sequence. 4. Continue clicking holes until you reach the **last** or **exit hole.** **** 5. To complete the sequence, **double-click** the final hole or press **Enter**. 6. An **editable lace pattern** will automatically generate in the 2D window for further modifications. **** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569352588569) #### **Edit Lacing** Edit the direction or curvature of an existing lacing without deleting and recreating it. 1. Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59494850587289) **Edit Lacing Tool** from the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click an **existing lacing** in the 2D/3D window to select it. 3. In the dialog, adjust the direction or curvature using the **Reverse** or **Curvature** options. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59494850587673) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55479973887385)** * **Reverse** * A **reverse icon** ![Reverse.svg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55445403327769)will appear attached to your cursor. * Click a specific hole to flip the lacing direction at that point. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55479973887385)** * **Curvature** * Use the slider to adjust the cord's arc. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59494870150681) Increasing curvature helps stabilise simulation by preventing the cord from colliding with or clipping into nearby patterns. **** **📝 Note:** The generated lace is a standard pattern piece; you can independently edit its thickness, material, or physical properties in the Property Editor like any other garment part. **✨ Tip:** If the cord enters an eyelet from the wrong side in 3D, use the **reverse icon** to flip the orientation without redrawing the entire path.
content_description: Discover the new **Define Path** and **Edit Lacing** features in 2026.0 that automate and customize your lacing patterns effortlessly, enhancing your design process.

title: Volume Measurement (Bag/Garment)
content: ## **New in 2026.1** **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642865482009)** **Select Target Patterns** **Edit Volume** **Measurement Properties** **Reset and Delete** **** _A volumetric calculation tool specifically engineered for bag and accessory development._ #### **Select Target Patterns** 1. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59645602459673) **Volume Measure (Garment/Bag)** tool from 3D Toolbar ▶ Inside the menu group of ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59645602460313) **Linear Measure (Garment)**. 2. Select the patterns that form the enclosed space of the bag from either the 2D or 3D windows. 3. Press the **Enter** key to confirm the pattern range and run the automated calculation. → In the 3D window, confirmed patterns are highlighted in Green. An orange measurement mesh is created inside the bag. → Display volume properties instantly in the Property Editor. #### #### **Edit Volume** 1. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59645625313561) **Edit Volume Measure (Garment/Bag)** tool from 3D Toolbar ▶ Inside the menu group of ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59645602463257) **Edit Measure (Garment)**. 2. Click on the orange measurement mesh to select the target volume block. → Display measurement properties instantly in the Property Editor. 3. Move the measurement mesh along the X, Y, or Z directions using the three standard directional arrows in the 3D window. 4. Click the **Scale button** on the tool for mesh resizing in the 3D window. 5. Click the **Scale button** again to exit back to standard Select/Move mesh mode. #### #### **Measurement Properties** 1. The following properties display in the Property Editor after confirming the pattern target, or whenever clicking on an existing measurement mesh. **Properties** | **Descriptions** ---|--- **Name** | Name of each volume. **Volume Measurement (L)** | Volume calculation result from the bag/garment’s measurement mesh. **Target Volume (L)** | Set the goal capacity value. **Tolerance (L)/(%)** | Sets the acceptable deviation range from the Target Volume. Example: If Target Volume is 10 L, and Tolerance is +/-2 L, the acceptable range is from 8 to 12 L. **Unit** | Set the tolerance measurement between Liters (L) or Percentage (%). **Mesh Scale** | Resize the measurement mesh in the 3D window. A higher value makes the mesh move outward. A Lower value makes the mesh move inward. #### **Reset and Delete** 1. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59645625313561) **Edit Volume Measure (Garment/Bag)** tool from 3D Toolbar ▶ Inside the menu group of ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59645602463257) **Edit Measure (Garment)**. 2. Right-click on the orange dummy mesh. 3. Select **Reset** to reset the measurement mesh back to its original position and scale values derived from the first calculation. 4. Select **Delete**(Shortcut: **Del**) to delete the selected measurement mesh and clear its properties. **📝****Note:** * _Volume dummy meshes do not automatically update when the pattern is edited or when a 3D Simulation is re-run. The mesh preserves its shape based on the state of the pattern when it was first calculated. This allows you to keep it as a constant design reference. To update the calculation, delete the existing mesh and measure the area again._
content_description: Discover the powerful volumetric calculation tool designed for streamlined bag and accessory development in Clo3D, featuring new functionalities for selecting target patterns, editing volume measurements, and managing properties with ease.

content: **List of Contents** Plot Patterns Recommended Plotter Specifications Plot 2D patterns to manufacture real garments. #### **Plot Patterns** 1\.
